page: Vultr vx1-g-32c-128g is an x86_64 cloud server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical AMD EPYC cores operating at 2.0 GHz, supporting two threads per core. The configuration includes 128.0 GB of memory, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, supported by 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. The instance includes a single complimentary public IPv4 address, operates without a GPU, and integrates 1 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate notable memory throughput and compression efficiency. In synthetic testing, memory bandwidth for large uncached write operations reached 195.06 GB/sec, placing it in the top 10% tier, alongside a PassMark memory score of 2993.05. Read throughput for large uncached blocks measured 295.05 GB/sec, ranking in the top 25%. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 40.52 GB/sec and single-threaded bzip3 decompression achieved 17.98 GB/sec, both scoring in the top 10%. Extended instruction capability is supported by instruction flags including AVX-512 (VNNI and BF16), SHA-NI, and VAES.

General multi-core processing registers in standard ranges, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 6176.0 and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 48789.2. However, the system demonstrates strong single-core stress-ng performance at 3056.39 and an overall PassMark CPU score of 62261.68. Lightweight CPU-based machine learning inference performs effectively, registering 475.28 tokens/sec for text generation on a 135M model and 52.68 tokens/sec on a 7B model. Static web serving throughput reached 80.02 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations achieved 62.56 million operations per second.

A primary trade-off of this server type is the 1 GB local NVMe SSD footprint, which restricts reliance on local disk for substantive data persistence and requires external network storage or specialized diskless configurations. The platform balances dedicated core allocation with strong memory throughput, making it suitable for memory-intensive caching layers, high-throughput static web serving, compression pipelines, and CPU-driven small model inference.
description: Vultr vx1-g-32c-128g is a general-purpose cloud instance equipped with 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical AMD EPYC cores clocked at 2.0 GHz. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, the platform supplies 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU, alongside 1 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and zero GPUs. Benchmark profiles reveal exceptional memory performance, with uncached write speeds reaching 195.06 GB/sec and a top-tier PassMark memory score of 2993.05. Processing capabilities are enhanced by AVX-512 and cryptographic extensions, showing strong results in single-threaded compression and CPU-based small LLM inference. Due to the minimal 1 GB local disk, this instance is suited for memory-heavy compute tasks, in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, compression pipelines, and distributed web serving clusters that leverage remote storage.
